I will think about this the way I always do — start from what I did last year, what my neighbors do, and what the land tells me.

My 4.1 mu is small. It is just me in the house now, so I cannot waste money, but I also cannot afford a bad harvest. At my age, the land must feed me. I plant wheat in October after I clear the maize, then summer maize in June right after wheat harvest — same as everyone in our village.

**Wheat (winter, about 4.1 mu):**
Last year I put down two bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15, 50 kg each) per mu before ploughing — that is my base. Then when the wheat greens up in spring, I top-dress with urea, about one bag (50 kg) for every 2-3 mu. That works out to roughly 25-28 kg of nitrogen per mu total. My neighbor old Zhang tried less last year and his wheat was yellow at jointing, so I will not cut back. I use improved seed from the agri-shop in town — the dealer sells what works here, Jimai or Shinong type. I irrigate from the well: once before winter so the roots set, once at green-up, once at jointing, once at grain filling. Four waterings. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew, usually twice. I rotary till — ploughing deep costs more to hire the tractor.

**Maize (summer, same 4.1 mu):**
After wheat I do not plough, just no-till and drill the maize seed right in — everyone does it this way now, saves time and the ground is already soft from wheat irrigation. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu type. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, then urea when it reaches knee-high, about 20-25 kg nitrogen per mu total. Maize does not need as much water here in summer — usually one irrigation if the rain is short. Spray once for borer.

I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than see thin ears. Fertilizer money you can see back in the harvest.
